Pareschi and Popa conjectured that Y has minimal cohomology class if and only if the structure sheaf of Y satisfies a property that they call M-regularity.   Let now X be a smooth cubic threefold. By a classical result due to Clemens and Griffiths, its intermediate Jacobian J(X) is a principally polarised abelian variety; furthermore the Fano surface of lines on X can be embedded in J(X) and has minimal cohomology class. In this short note we show that its structure sheaf is M-regular.

outputs.L1: Let \((A,\Theta)\) be a principally polarised abelian variety, and let \(Y\subseteq A\) be a subvariety. Pareschi and Popa conjectured that \(Y\) has minimal cohomology class if and only if its structure sheaf satisfies a property known as \(M\)-regularity. Now let \(X\) be a smooth cubic threefold. A classical result of Clemens and Griffiths establishes that its intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\) is a principally polarised abelian variety. Moreover, the Fano surface of lines on \(X\) embeds into \(J(X)\) and has minimal cohomology class. In this short note, we prove that its structure sheaf is \(M\)-regular.
outputs.L2: Given a principally polarized abelian variety \((A,\Theta)\) and a subvariety \(Y\subseteq A\), Pareschi and Popa proposed that \(Y\) represents a minimal cohomology class precisely when its structure sheaf is M-regular. Now suppose that \(X\) is a smooth cubic threefold. A classical theorem of Clemens and Griffiths states that the intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\) carries a principal polarization. Moreover, the Fano surface parametrizing lines contained in \(X\) embeds into \(J(X)\) and represents a minimal cohomology class. This note proves that the structure sheaf of this Fano surface is indeed M-regular.
outputs.L3:
Pareschi and Popa conjectured a close relationship between the geometry of subvarieties of principally polarised abelian varieties and the generic vanishing properties of their structure sheaves. More precisely, if \(Y\) is a \(d\)-dimensional subvariety of a principally polarised abelian variety \((A,\Theta)\) of dimension \(g\), then \(Y\) is said to have minimal cohomology class when
\[
[Y]=\frac{\Theta^{g-d}}{(g-d)!}.
\]
Their conjecture predicts that this numerical minimality is equivalent to the M-regularity of the structure sheaf of \(Y\), viewed as a coherent sheaf on \(A\). M-regularity is a strong generic-vanishing condition expressed in terms of the cohomological support loci of the sheaf.

A particularly important example arises from a smooth cubic threefold \(X\). Its intermediate Jacobian \(J(X)\) is a five-dimensional principally polarised abelian variety. The Fano surface \(F(X)\), parametrising the lines contained in \(X\), is a smooth projective surface and admits a natural Abel–Jacobi embedding
\[
F(X)\hookrightarrow J(X).
\]
Under this embedding, the Fano surface has minimal cohomology class:
\[
[F(X)]=\frac{\Theta^{3}}{3!}.
\]

The note establishes the corresponding generic-vanishing property by proving that the structure sheaf \(\mathcal O_{F(X)}\), regarded as a sheaf on \(J(X)\), is M-regular. Thus, the Fano surface of a smooth cubic threefold provides a significant example supporting the Pareschi–Popa conjectural characterization of subvarieties with minimal cohomology class.
outputs.L4:
Let \((A,\Theta)\) be a principally polarized abelian variety of dimension \(g\), and let \(X\subset A\) be a subvariety of dimension \(d\). Pareschi and Popa conjectured a close relationship between two extremal properties of \(X\): the geometric condition that \(X\) represent the minimal cohomology class
\[
[X]=\frac{\theta^{g-d}}{(g-d)!},
\]
where \(\theta=c_1(\Theta)\), and the cohomological condition that its structure sheaf \(\mathcal O_X\), regarded as a sheaf on \(A\), be \(M\)-regular. In terms of the cohomological support loci
\[
V^i(\mathcal O_X)=\{\alpha\in \operatorname{Pic}^0(A)\mid
H^i(X,\mathcal O_X\otimes \alpha)\neq 0\},
\]
\(M\)-regularity means that
\[
\operatorname{codim}_{\operatorname{Pic}^0(A)}V^i(\mathcal O_X)>i
\qquad\text{for every }i>0.
\]
The conjecture therefore predicts that minimality of the cohomology class is reflected in especially strong generic-vanishing properties.

The note studies this prediction for one of the principal classical examples of a subvariety with minimal cohomology class. Let \(Y\subset \mathbf P^4\) be a smooth cubic threefold, let \(F\) be its Fano surface parametrizing lines contained in \(Y\), and let \(J(Y)\) denote the intermediate Jacobian of \(Y\). The Abel–Jacobi map embeds \(F\) into the five-dimensional principally polarized abelian variety \(J(Y)\). Under this embedding, the class of \(F\) is
\[
[F]=\frac{\theta^3}{3!},
\]
so \(F\) is a surface of minimal cohomology class in \(J(Y)\).

The main result is that the sheaf \(\mathcal O_F\), viewed as a coherent sheaf on \(J(Y)\), is \(M\)-regular. Equivalently, its higher cohomological support loci satisfy the strict codimension inequalities required by \(M\)-regularity. The proof analyzes the cohomology of topologically trivial twists of \(\mathcal O_F\) and uses the geometry of the Fano surface together with its Abel–Jacobi embedding.

Thus the Fano surface exhibits precisely the behavior predicted by Pareschi and Popa: its minimal cohomology class is accompanied by the \(M\)-regularity of its structure sheaf. This verifies the conjectured correspondence in a fundamental example and further demonstrates how the geometry of special subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties is encoded by generic-vanishing phenomena.
outputs.L5:
Let \((A,\Theta)\) be a principally polarized abelian variety, where \(\Theta\) denotes a theta divisor. Theta divisors play a central role in the geometry of abelian varieties because they encode both the polarization and important information about the underlying variety.

Work by Giuseppe Pareschi, often in collaboration with Mihnea Popa, developed powerful methods for studying line bundles and coherent sheaves on abelian varieties. Their theory of generic vanishing and \(M\)-regularity provides criteria for global generation, multiplication maps, and projective embeddings. In this setting, the positivity of multiples of \(\Theta\) can be analyzed through the vanishing of cohomology after twisting by line bundles in \(\operatorname{Pic}^0(A)\).

Thus, if we let \(L=\mathcal O_A(\Theta)\), the properties of \(L^{\otimes m}\) illustrate how theta geometry, Fourier–Mukai techniques, and Pareschi’s results combine to describe the projective geometry of \(A\).

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the connection between the Pareschi–Popa conjecture, minimal cohomology classes, and the Fano surface embedded in the intermediate Jacobian of a cubic threefold.
counterfactuals.output:
The Pareschi–Popa conjecture links **generic vanishing** on a principally polarized abelian variety \((A,\Theta)\) with the notion of a **minimal cohomology class**. For a geometrically nondegenerate \(d\)-dimensional subvariety \(Z\subset A\), the minimal possible class is

\[
[Z]=\frac{\Theta^{g-d}}{(g-d)!},
\qquad g=\dim A.
\]

Pareschi and Popa predict that subvarieties whose twisted ideal sheaf \(\mathcal I_Z(\Theta)\) satisfies the GV condition are precisely the special minimal-class subvarieties. This fits with the related classification conjecture of Debarre: apart from the standard loci \(W_d(C)\) in Jacobians of curves, the only exceptional minimal-class example should be the **Fano surface of lines on a smooth cubic threefold**.

Indeed, if \(Y\subset \mathbf P^4\) is a smooth cubic threefold, its Fano surface \(F(Y)\) embeds via the Abel–Jacobi map into the five-dimensional intermediate Jacobian \(J(Y)\). With its principal polarization \(\Theta\),

\[
[F(Y)]=\frac{\Theta^3}{3!},
\]

so \(F(Y)\) has minimal cohomology class; moreover, \(\mathcal I_{F(Y)}(\Theta)\) has the expected generic-vanishing behavior. Thus the Fano surface is the fundamental non-Jacobian model in the Pareschi–Popa picture: generic vanishing singles out minimal classes, and minimal classes are expected to force either Jacobian geometry or this cubic-threefold/intermediate-Jacobian geometry.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

Building on this description, we prove that the natural theta-twisted ideal sheaf \(\mathcal I_{F(X)}(2\Theta)\) is \(M\)-regular on \(J(X)\).

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a research-paper abstract about verifying one direction of the Pareschi–Popa conjecture for the Fano surface of lines on a smooth cubic threefold.
counterfactuals.output:
Let \(Y\subset \mathbf P^{4}\) be a smooth cubic threefold, \(F(Y)\) its Fano surface of lines, and \(J(Y)\) the intermediate Jacobian with its principal polarization \(\Theta\). Via the Abel–Jacobi embedding, \(F(Y)\) represents the minimal cohomology class \(\Theta^{3}/3!\). We verify the corresponding direction of the Pareschi–Popa conjecture by proving that the theta-twisted ideal sheaf
\[
\mathcal I_{F(Y)}(\Theta)

is a GV-sheaf on \(J(Y)\). Equivalently, its cohomological support loci satisfy
\[
\operatorname{codim}_{\operatorname{Pic}^{0}(J(Y))}V^{i}\!\left(\mathcal I_{F(Y)}(\Theta)\right)\ge i
\qquad\text{for all }i>0.

The proof combines the geometry of the Abel–Jacobi embedding with generic-vanishing and Fourier–Mukai techniques. Incidence correspondences between lines on \(Y\), together with the relation between the Fano surface and the theta divisor of \(J(Y)\), are used to control the relevant twisted cohomology groups and their jumping loci. Thus the Fano surface provides the exceptional five-dimensional example, alongside subvarieties of Jacobians, predicted by the Pareschi–Popa framework: its minimal cohomology class is accompanied by the expected generic-vanishing property.
